$comment: What the graph holds of an annotation and of a resource, as every implementation of the graph's two codecs must say it. TypeScript (@semiont/graph: annotation-codec.ts, resource-codec.ts) and Python (semiont_graph: codec.py) each run every case, and a third implementation would. A store keeps its own dialect (a map set on a node, a chain of properties, a list kept as a JSON string); what is stored, what each stored thing is called, which are required and what is refused are stated here, once. Each case has one of six parts. `annotationStored`: an annotation as the record gives it; the `properties` of its row that are plain strings; the properties that are JSON, each given under `json` as the value the stored string must parse to (a serializer is free in its spacing and its key order); its `tags`, which are edges and not properties, as a set; the resource it `linksTo`, where the reference edge goes; and what the graph `holds`, which is what reading the row back answers. `annotationRead`: a row's `properties` (JSON ones as the strings a store holds) and its `tags` in whatever order a store answers them, and the `annotation` read. `annotationUpdated`: the `current` annotation as the graph holds it, the `updates`, and the `annotation` the update leaves; a store writes that annotation whole. `referenceResolved`: the `current` annotation, the `source` it is resolved to, and the `body` it then has. `resourceStored` and `resourceRead` say the same of a resource. Where an implementation must refuse, the part has `refused`: a word the refusal names (the missing field, or the resource an update tried to move to). An annotation a case gives is as a read answers it, with a person named; the graph's side of every case holds that person without the name. Text here is carried and never counted, so a character outside the basic plane is in the table to be carried as itself. Add a case here before changing an implementation.

cases.why: a highlight is its row and nothing else: no link, no tags, and the quoted text pulled out beside the selector. Who it is by is stored as who, without a person's name: the name is the directory's, which a read joins on and a person can change
a link to a resource is the `source` property, which is also where the reference edge goes; a target that is a whole resource stores no selector at all
entity tags are edges, not properties, and are held in one order whatever order they were written in: sorted, then the link
the graph holds what its queries need and no more: an annotation's attribution and a comment's text are the views' to keep
when it was changed and the software that made it are carried; a body that is one item and not a list is read as that one item
a selector is carried as given, a list of selectors as a list, and a character outside the basic plane as itself: the codec counts nothing
an empty body is no body: nothing is stored for it and none is read back
a row and its tag edges are read as the annotation: tags first, in the one order, then the link
a tag edge with no name is no tag
a row with no id is refused, by that name: a required field is never given a value the row does not hold
a row with no resourceId is refused, by that name: a required field is never given a value the row does not hold
a row with no creator is refused, by that name: a required field is never given a value the row does not hold
a row with no motivation is refused, by that name: a required field is never given a value the row does not hold
a row with no created is refused, by that name: a required field is never given a value the row does not hold
an update leaves the current annotation with the changed fields replaced: here its whole body
a body updated to nothing takes the link and the tags with it
a field the update does not name is unchanged
a selector may change; the resource it is on may not
an annotation belongs to one resource for good: an update that names another is refused
an update cannot rename an annotation: the id stays the one it was made under
resolving a reference replaces its link and keeps its tags
a reference with no body yet is resolved to the link alone
a resource is its name, entity types, format, checksum, storage location, whether it is archived, when the record says it was created and who the record says it is by
a representation stored nowhere has no storage property at all, and none is read back
a resource with no archived flag is not archived, and one with no entity types has none; one party it is by is stored as the one
the graph holds of a resource what its queries need and no more: a description, a draft flag and a byte size are the views' to keep
a resource with no name is refused on the way in, by that name, rather than stored as a row that could not be read back
a resource with no dateCreated is refused on the way in, by that name, rather than stored as a row that could not be read back
a resource with no wasAttributedTo is refused on the way in, by that name, rather than stored as a row that could not be read back
a resource with no representations is refused on the way in, by that name, rather than stored as a row that could not be read back
a resource with no checksum is refused on the way in, by that name, rather than stored as a row that could not be read back
a row is read as the resource, with its one representation rebuilt
false and an empty list are values a row holds, not absence
a row with no id is refused, by that name
a row with no name is refused, by that name
a row with no entityTypes is refused, by that name
a row with no format is refused, by that name
a row with no archived is refused, by that name
a row with no created is refused, by that name
a row with no creator is refused, by that name
a row with no contentChecksum is refused, by that name
